node.text:
FunctionGemma allows developers to run function-calling LLMs entirely on-device. At only 270M parameters, the model is compact enough to run efficiently on mobile hardware without needing an internet connection.

For AI engineers, moving inference to the edge addresses critical latency and privacy constraints. First, it eliminates network latency since the processing happens directly on the device’s CPU. Second, it removes per-token API costs associated with cloud models. Finally, it ensures data privacy by keeping user inputs and logic offline.

You can fine-tune the base model on your specific tools, quantize it, and deploy it using MediaPipe or LiteRT. You can test the performance yourself by searching for AI Edge Gallery in the app store, or look up FunctionGemma 270M / Mobile Actions on Hugging Face to access the weights and fine-tuning notebooks.

#llm #aiengineering #aiagents #freetools #opensource

node.text:
Comment ‘3d’ to learn how I made this. God’s eye view 24-hour replay of Operation Epic Fury.

The Iran strikes kicked off and I set an AI agent swarm loose to record every OSINT signal I could find before the caches cleared. Built a full 4D reconstruction in WorldView.

I can scrub through minute by minute and watch the whole thing unfold on a 3D globe:

> Airspace clearing over Tehran
> Ground strike coordinates locking in
> Severe GPS interference blinding the region
> EO and SAR satellites making passes over the strike zone
> No-fly zones locking down 9 countries
> Shipping fleets scrambling at the Strait of Hormuz

It’s pretty amazing how complete of a picture you can build without “proprietary data fusion” — one dev with public signals and a love for computer graphics and geospatial intelligence.

Thank you for all the love on my last post. Dropping WorldView in April. This my friends is just the beginning.

#ai #3d #photogrammetry #futuretech #osint

Everything is fair in love and war 😂❤️

node.text:
To disprove the myth that piranhas are instant “crusher machines,” biologist and presenter Jeremy Wade conducted one of the most famous experiments on the River Monsters program.

He got into a pool full of red-bellied piranhas (Pygocentrus nattereri), which had been deprived of food, to show that they do not attack humans without a specific stimulus, such as blood or a frantic movement of agony.

Wade showed that the predatory behavior of these fish is actually opportunistic and defensive. In the wild, piranhas act as “cleaners” of rivers, feeding on carron or injured animals.

The collective panic around them has historically been fueled by exaggerated accounts, including a visit by Theodore Roosevelt to Brazil. Wade’s experiment showed that, in the absence of blood in the water or extreme drought conditions, when food is scarce and aggressiveness increases, they prefer to keep their distance from a large and calm animal like humans.

In this account you learn every day something you didn’t know... or

*دنیا میں %95 لوگ اس لیئے پریشان ھیں کیونکہ انہوں نے انویسٹمنٹ (Investment) کبھی سیکھی ھی نہیں…*
💡 مسئلہ کہاں ھے؟
*اکثر لوگ ساری زندگی صرف آمدن (Income) بڑھانے میں لگے رہتے ھیں*
*لیکن کبھی سرمایہ کاری (Investment) نہیں سیکھتے*
👈 *نتیجہ کیا نکلتا ھے؟*
جتنی آمدن بڑھتی ھے ، اتنے ھی اخراجات بھی بڑھ جاتے ھیں
مہنگائی (Inflation) پیسے کی ویلیو کھا جاتی ھے
اور بندہ ساری زندگی " کام " کرتا رہتا ھے… پیسے کو کام پر نہیں لگاتا
📈 *اصل گیم کیا ھے؟*
اصل گیم پیسہ کمانا نہیں… پیسہ بڑھانا ھے
👈 *پیسہ بڑھتا کیسے ھے؟*
جب آپ اسے انویسٹمنٹ (Investment) میں لگاتے ھیں
بینک میں پیسہ رکھنے سے ویلیو کم ہوتی ھے
لیکن صحیح جگہ انویسٹ کرنے سے پیسہ Multiply ہوتا ھے
🚀 *سٹاک مارکیٹ کیوں ضروری ھے؟*
پاکستان سٹاک ایکسچینج صرف ایک مارکیٹ نہیں…
یہ وہ جگہ ھے جہاں:
👈 آپ گھر بیٹھے کمپنیوں میں حصے دار Partner بن سکتے ھیں
👈 آپ کا پیسہ آپ کے لیئے کام کرتا ھے
👈 آپ کو منافع (Profit) اور ڈیویڈینڈ (Dividend) دونوں مل سکتے ھیں
🌍 *امیر لوگ کیا کرتے ھیں؟*
دنیا کے بڑے بڑے انویسٹرز جیسے
وارن بفیٹ Warren Buffett
نے اپنی دولت کا بڑا حصہ سٹاک مارکیٹ سے بنایا
👈 فرق صرف ایک ھے:
انہوں نے انویسٹمنٹ سیکھی… باقی لوگ صرف کماتے رھے
🔥 حقیقت جو کوئی نہیں بتاتا
پیسہ کمانا مشکل نہیں ھے
لیکن…
پیسے کو بڑھانا سب سے مشکل کام ھے
*اور یہ صرف ایک Skill سے آتا ھے:*
*اور وہ Skill ھے ۔۔ انویسٹمنٹ (Investment)*
⏳ اب فیصلہ آپ کا ھے

❌ ساری زندگی کام کریں… اور پیسے کے پیچھے بھاگتے رہیں

How to find your contrast level!

Your contrast level is basically the difference between the lightest and darkest parts of your features and knowing yours can make a HUGE difference. 

When you dress with your natural contrast, your outfits actually compliment your natural colouring

Here’s how to figure yours out:
Step 1: take a photo of yourself in natural light (no makeup if you can!) and convert it to black & white (use the saturation tool not a filter)
Step 2: Find the lightest and darkest parts of your features and place them on my contrast scale (link in bio)
Step 3: Subtract the lowest number from the highest and that’s your contrast level!

🤍 Low contrast (1 - 3) your features are close in tone. You look good in tonal outfits, blended colour palettes and monochromatic looks. Avoid super harsh colour blocking!

🩶 Medium contrast (4 - 7) you’ve got a beautiful balance. You can wear both tonal and contrasting outfits, lucky you!

🖤 High contrast (8 - 10) you’ve got striking, bold features. You were made for high contrast outfits so like  black & white, bold colour blocking and sharp patterns.

Also the most common question I get is can I use the whites of my eyes?! They’re part of your face so they count! BUT this is where people get tripped up, not everyone’s whites are actually that white! Some are more ivory or warm toned, so don’t just assume you are a specific contrast level without testing it on the scale.

Drop your number below 👇 I’d love to know!

Beauty is a biopolitical regime that sorts, ranks, and disciplines bodies. To interrogate the politics of beauty is to confront the broader question of which bodies are allowed to exist freely, and which are consigned to erasure.

Beauty standards operate as a form of aesthetic governance, delineating who is considered worthy of protection, whose suffering is acknowledged, and whose lives are marked as grievable. Its about power, recognition, and the uneven distribution of humanity itself.

But this time, it was necessary to respond to the Taliban. If we had not shown strength, they would have considered us weak. I do not support wars, but in this situation, it was necessary to give a response.

Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq (often called Mard-e-Mujahid) supported the Afghan jihad against the Soviet Union in the 1980s, aligning with the United States and Saudi Arabia, which brought Pakistan significant military and financial aid while strengthening his domestic power through Islamization. Pervez Musharraf initially maintained links with certain militant groups but, after 9/11, joined the U.S.-led War on Terror, a move that secured billions of dollars in aid and international political support, while also helping him consolidate authority at home. Historically, both leaders’ jihad-related policies were shaped not only by ideology but also by strategic interests, financial incentives, and the pursuit of political power, with long-lasting consequences for the region.

#🇺🇸 Los Angeles is painting its streets white
☀️
To combat extreme heat waves and the “urban heat island” effect, LA is coating its black asphalt roads with a special solar reflective paint. This simple hack bounces the sun’s rays back into space instead of absorbing them, dropping street-level temperatures by up to 15 degrees. It’s a massive, real-world experiment to cool down the city and save lives during brutal summers🌡️🏙️

This iconic scene is from the long-running comedy sketch show Saturday Night Live (SNL).
Specifically, it is from the recurring sketch titled "The Roxbury Guys" (also known as the "What Is Love" sketch). While the sketch appeared multiple times with different hosts, the footage in your video features Jim Carrey alongside series regulars Will Ferrell and Chris Kattan.
Ils font vraiment le trio a trois 😂😂😂😂😂

node.text: @yogisyed "Pakistan has no future without Imran Khan.
@yogisyed "Pakistan has no future without Imran Khan.

Most people waste their bored moments. Curious people use them to think differently.

Here are 25+ theories that will reshape how you approach problems, decisions, and systems at work:

→ Goodhart’s Law

When a measure becomes a target, it stops being useful. Sound familiar in your KPIs? 

→ Chesterton’s Fence 

Never remove a process until you understand why it exists. 

→ The Lindy Effect 

If something has lasted 100 years, bet on it lasting 100 more. 

→ Hofstadter’s Law 

Every project takes longer than expected. Even when you plan for that.

The best leaders I know aren’t just experienced, they’re conceptually fluent.

They have frameworks for why things fail, why systems break, and why people behave the way they do.
This carousel is a starting point.

Which of these theories do you already use in your work? Drop it in the comments 👇

🚨 5 Illegal Ways Hackers Make Money (Part 1) 💻💸

⚠️ Disclaimer: This video is strictly for educational purposes only.

1️⃣ Cryptojacking
A crypto farm is basically a server farm that runs hundreds of crypto transactions. On every transaction, a small percentage is earned as a reward. But setting up powerful servers is expensive.

This is where hackers step in. They know the whole game is about compute power ⚡
Instead of buying expensive hardware, they secretly steal small amounts of processing power from thousands of normal devices.
How?

They create a website or distribute pirated software or movies embedded with malicious crypto-mining code. Once someone installs or runs it, the hidden code starts working in the background, performing tiny calculations for mining — usually without the user noticing.
Individually, it’s small.
But multiply that by thousands of devices… and it becomes equivalent to a small server farm. 💰
This gives hackers a regular income stream without spending a single dime.
👇 Comment “Crypto” + your favorite movie to get the full breakdown.

🔥 Follow @podus.app for Part 2.

Beshak SubhanAllah Alhamdulillah ALLAH HU AKBAR ❤️
He is the Imam Mahdi Sp Patani Para Karnan Last Messiah 666

Jo log soch rahe hain ki Ramadan 2026 me ye signs complete ho gaye, ye unke liye hai.
According to the narration attributed to Imam Jaʿfar al-Sadiq. In Sunan al-Daraqutni (Kitab al-Eidain, Hadith 1881–1882 in some editions) ek report mention karti hai ki Imam Mahdi ke zahoor se pehle Ramadan me do unusual eclipses honge:
• Mahine ke shuru me lunar eclipse
• Mahine ke beech me solar eclipse
Lekin Ramadan 2026 me iska opposite hua — pehle solar eclipse aya aur baad me lunar eclipse, isliye jo condition us narration me mention hai wo fulfill nahi hui.
Scientifically bhi ye order actually normal hai. Solar eclipse sirf new moon par hota hai, aur lunar eclipse sirf full moon par hota hai. In dono phases ke beech lagbhag 14–15 din ka gap hota hai. Isi liye usually solar eclipse mahine ke pehle part me aur lunar eclipse baad me aata hai.
Isliye 2026 ke eclipses normal astronomical pattern follow kar rahe the, na ki ye sign jo narration me describe kiya gaya hai. Ye unusual sign hai.

Those who're thinking these signs completed in Ramadan 2026 so this is for you all... According to the narration attributed to Imam Jaʿfar al-Sadiq. In Sunan al-Daraqutni (Kitab al-Eidain, Hadith 1881–1882 in some editions) a report mentions that before the appearance of Imam Mahdi there will be two unusual eclipses in Ramadan:
• A lunar eclipse at the beginning of the month
• A solar eclipse in the middle of the month
But in Ramadan 2026 the opposite happened — the solar eclipse came first and the lunar eclipse came later, so the condition mentioned in that narration was not fulfilled.
Scientifically, this order is actually normal. A solar eclipse only happens at a new moon, while a lunar eclipse only happens at a full moon, and these phases are about 14–15 days apart. That’s why a solar eclipse usually occurs earlier in the month and a lunar eclipse later.
So the 2026 eclipses followed the normal astronomical pattern, not the unusual sign described in the narration. And Allah S.W.T knows more.

خان پور : ڈی ایس پی آفس اکٹھ پر آنے والی خاتون کے مبینہ اغوا کی کوشش 

خان پور : بااثر افراد نے خواتین کے ہمراہ ڈی ایس پی آفس نے نزدیک اغوا کی کوشش کی 

خان پور : واقعہ کی سی سی ٹی وی فوٹیج اے آر وائی نیوز کو موصول ہو گئی 

خان پور : فوٹیج میں متاثرہ نسیم بی بی کا راستہ روکتے واضح دیکھا جا سکتا ہے 

خان پور : میرے خاوند غلام حسین کے ساتھ میرا تنازعہ چل رہا ہے ، متاثرہ نسیم بی بی 

خان پور : خاوند کے رشتے داروں نے اکٹھ سے واپسی پر اغوا کرنے کی کوشش کی ، متاثرہ خاتون 

خان پور : سٹی پولیس نے مقدمہ تو درج کیا لیکن اصل ملزمان کو کام بوجھ کر فرار ہونے کا موقع دیا ، متاثرہ خاتون 

خان پور : سٹی پولیس ملزمان کو فیور دینا چاہتی ہے ، متاثرہ خاتون 

خان پور : ڈی پی او رحیم یارخان نوٹس لے کر انصاف مہیا کریں ، خاتون کی اپیل

node.text:
Do you like this kind of new format? 👇 Vote above.

Before you sleep in an Airbnb…
you might want to understand how hackers see a network.

Sometimes what appears online…
is hiding in the room.

Most exposed cameras aren’t hacked.
They’re just left open.

Learn how networks really work.

Link in bio.

#cybersecurity #cyber #hacker #linux #engineering
I’m taking a networking program… Looks like I’ll learn more here

anyone with a brain running an airbnb isn't going to have security devices on the same network they give the guests. It's not hard to setup a 2nd network without broadcasting the SSID. I'm pretty sure even the old actiontec I had 20 years ago had that function.

@remy.engineering we are not a fbi agent who will be monitored by hackers. A average human is never the target of hackers at return on investment is very low. They always target High net worth individual, businessman, corporate officials etc and they already have a security team to handle this.

@giorgosx_ I swear down.
The narration of the visuals is just fascinating whilst bit terrifying

node.text: My project list for the next few weeks 💻

Most developers focus on writing code.

Very few focus on how that code fits into a system.

And that’s where the real difference is.

Because in real-world engineering,
your impact is not decided by how many lines you write…

It’s decided by:
👉 How your system scales
👉 How easy it is to maintain
👉 How well different parts work together

That’s architecture.

The same feature can be built in multiple ways,
but only one design will survive at scale.

If you understand these architectures,
you won’t just build projects…

You’ll start thinking like an engineer who builds production systems.

Don’t just code features.
Design systems. 🚀

Save this — this is what actually levels you up.

node.text:
Numbers in this video are rough estimates to build intuition, not exact figures.

In reality, training cost depends on many factors like dataset size and quality, number of tokens, model architecture, hardware setup (type and number of GPUs), system efficiency, parallelization strategy, and how many times you retrain or tune the model.

Also, training doesn’t happen on a single GPU. Large models are trained on hundreds or even thousands of GPUs in parallel. So instead of one GPU running for 30,000 hours, it’s many GPUs running together for a much shorter time.

GPU pricing also varies a lot depending on provider, availability, and scale. The $3/hour number is not universal.

Another important point: model performance is not just about the number of parameters. Data quality, architecture design, and training techniques matter just as much, if not more.

Even reported numbers like GPT-4’s parameter count are not officially confirmed, so take such figures as approximations.

So don’t take the exact numbers literally. Focus on the bigger idea: building large AI models requires massive compute, high-quality data, and multiple iterations.

“This happens because the Earth is a sphere, but maps like the Mercator projection flatten it onto a 2D surface. To preserve angles for navigation, distances and sizes get distorted—especially near the poles, where regions appear stretched. So even though two paths may look similar or misleading on a flat map, their actual distances on the curved Earth can be very different.”

In the realm of digital chaos, few things are as terrifyingly impressive as the "zip bomb." This viral Discord screenshot features a user who has allegedly created a file named funny.zip that decompresses to a staggering **55.4 Yottabytes**. To put that into perspective, the post notes that as of 2016, total global internet traffic was only about **1.1 Zettabytes** per year. This tiny 42 KB file contains enough recursive data to effectively "explode" any hardware that attempts to unextract it, filling up storage space until the system crashes.
While it’s often used as a legendary internet prank, the zip bomb is a masterclass in data compression and a stark reminder that you should never trust a random download—no matter how "funny" it claims to be. In 2026, where our lives are entirely cloud-based, a 55-yottabyte file is basically a digital black hole. Download with caution, or your hard drive might just retire early!

Get ratings @umax.app [follow @ascend.maxx ]
. 
. 
. 
Blackpill (in the looksmaxxing context) is an online ideology that says a person’s life outcomes, especially dating and social respect, are mainly determined by genetics and physical appearance like facial structure and height, with self improvement having very limited impact beyond a fixed “genetic ceiling.” Followers often believe traits such as confidence, personality, fitness, or grooming do not significantly change how others perceive you if your base looks are low. In looksmaxxing spaces, blackpill ideas appear through terms like “Chad,” “mogging,” and looks ratings, often spread through dark humor memes and reels. Although looks do matter in first impressions, the blackpill view is widely criticized for being overly negative and harmful, especially for teenagers, as it can damage self esteem and ignore the real influence of mindset, health, effort, and social skills over time.
. 
. 
.

. 
Blackpill (in the looksmaxxing context) is an online ideology that says a person’s life outcomes, especially dating and social respect, are mainly determined by genetics and physical appearance like facial structure and height, with self improvement having very limited impact beyond a fixed “genetic ceiling.” Followers often believe traits such as confidence, personality, fitness, or grooming do not significantly change how others perceive you if your base looks are low. In looksmaxxing spaces, blackpill ideas appear through terms like “Chad,” “mogging,” and looks ratings, often spread through dark humor memes and reels. Although looks do matter in first impressions, the blackpill view is widely criticized for being overly negative and harmful, especially for teenagers, as it can damage self esteem and ignore the real influence of mindset, health, effort, and social skills over time.
. 
. 
.

Did you know that 7 out of 10 retirees can't keep their homes clean even when they have all day? They sit down "just for a minute" and three hours disappear. A neuroscientist says it's because their brains are protecting them from feeling overwhelmed. There's finally a simple fix that actually works. 

👉🏼 Read about breakthrough here
I’m a big clean as you go person.
Hi @katecohenfineart! It's wonderful that you practice the 'clean as you go' method. That's a fantastic way to prevent buildup and keep things feeling manageable. Thanks for sharing your approach!
Thanks for posting.  I have read about the exact methods where someone said it was a Japanese way of doing it. Perhaps both of them have the same method.
Hadn't heard of this before as "a thing" until I started doing it slowly a few years ago. Slow but sure.
Hi @skaldic44! It's wonderful to hear that you've found success with a similar approach over the past few years. Slow and steady progress can be so rewarding!
Are there no people with ADHD in Finland???

Yeah… I don’t think here in Finland we ALL have this cleanlines in our lives. This is not why Finland is happiest. We just don’t hope so much from life. We don’t have more or do things better. We are just content for less.
I used to work in McDonalds. They called it ‘clean as toy go’, to stay on top of things.

I have ALWAYS  hated cleaning, it just gets more & more depressing until I"m released to do something else, and never looks good so I have to settle for "better". I hope this method makes it more tolerable, now that I'm a senior & there isn't as much "something else" to DO.

AI B2B SaaS startups are now being built by younger founders faster than ever before.
Many of these teams launch products early, focus on solving niche business problems, and prioritize traction even before turning profitable.

This reflects a shift in how modern startups are built. Investors today often look beyond early profitability and focus on product-market fit, speed of execution, and the size of the opportunity — especially in fast-growing sectors like AI.

For founders, the lesson is clear:
Early-stage success is less about immediate profits and more about proving demand. Building something useful that people adopt quickly often matters more than perfect financials in the beginning.

Quant hedge funds rely on a mix of statistical and mathematical models to identify alpha and manage risk. Core tools include linear and multiple regression models for factor exposure and prediction, ARIMA and GARCH models for time-series forecasting and volatility clustering, Kalman filters for state estimation in dynamic systems, and cointegration tests such as Engle-Granger or Johansen for pairs trading. Portfolio construction often uses mean-variance optimization, Black-Litterman, and risk-parity frameworks, while risk is measured with Value at Risk (VaR), Expected Shortfall, and Monte Carlo simulation. More advanced firms apply machine learning models including random forests, gradient boosting, support vector machines, and deep neural networks for signal extraction, alongside hidden Markov models and regime-switching models to detect market states.

A data career isn’t a single role anymore.

It’s an ecosystem.

Different layers, different skills, all working together.

Here’s how the modern data world is structured 👇

- Core roles
Turning data into value through roles like analysts, engineers, and AI builders who handle everything from insights to production systems.

- Data engineering
Moving, transforming, and preparing data so it’s clean, reliable, and always available for downstream use.

- Data science & ML
Building models that learn patterns, make predictions, and solve complex problems using data.

- Analytics & BI
Presenting data in a way that drives decisions through dashboards, reports, and business-friendly insights.

- AI & LLM engineering
Creating intelligent applications using LLMs, agents, embeddings, and modern AI architectures.

- Cloud & infrastructure
Providing scalable systems and platforms where data storage, processing, and AI workloads run efficiently.

- DataOps & governance
Ensuring data is accurate, secure, traceable, and compliant across the entire lifecycle.

- Foundation skills
Core technical skills like SQL, Python, Git, and Linux that support every layer in the data stack.

What this means:
Your role is just one layer.
Your growth depends on understanding the stack around it.

Go deep in one area.
Stay aware of the entire system.

Which layer are you building depth in right now?

How Satellites 📡 Are Hacked by Hackers

Satellite systems are not just space infrastructure — they are part of the invisible cyber backbone of the modern world.
From GPS navigation to military communication and global internet routing, everything depends on signals traveling through open space and complex ground networks. From a hacker’s perspective, any system that relies on wireless transmission, trust-based communication, and layered protocols becomes an exploitable surface.

Attackers don’t “break into space” — they study signals, analyze communication patterns, and target weak points in ground stations, misconfigurations, and outdated security implementations.

The real risk is not the satellite itself — it’s the ecosystem built around it.

Understanding this layer means understanding how modern cyber-physical systems truly work.

This viral exchange perfectly captures the age-old debate regarding how early exposure to specific operating systems shapes our cognitive development and technical troubleshooting abilities. The original poster, Annie, suggests a correlation study between children raised on Mac versus Windows computers to see if one leads to higher tech illiteracy or weaker problem-solving skills later in life. The underlying theory is that "walled garden" ecosystems might stifle the curiosity required to understand how systems actually function. However, the thread takes a hilarious and sharp turn when a user mentions installing Linux at age twelve—a feat of digital endurance that usually involves hours of troubleshooting and terminal commands. Annie’s quick-witted reply about excluding certain demographics from the study to avoid skewing the data highlights a popular internet trope: the "tech wizard" archetype. It’s a witty commentary on how we learn to navigate the digital world and the different paths to computer literacy.

Most businesses don’t struggle with traffic.
They struggle with weak offers.

You can have the best marketing, the best content, and still not convert,  because the offer itself isn’t strong enough.

BRAND BY SID

How to make an offer people can’t refuse.

It starts with foundation.
You need deep clarity on your ideal client, their biggest problems, and the exact outcome they want. If this isn’t clear, everything else feels generic.

Then comes value creation.
Your offer should promise a clear transformation, not just a service. Add bonuses, stack value, and make the perception of what they’re getting feel far greater than what they’re paying.

Next is offer structure.
Keep it simple. Specific deliverables. Clear pricing. Strong guarantees. Confusion kills conversions — clarity closes deals.

Then comes presentation.
Your headline, your messaging, your copy. Focus on benefits, not features. Remove objections before they come up. Create urgency so people actually act.

But the real difference is in execution.

You research the market.
Position your offer differently.
Design it around outcomes.
Write copy that makes it easy to say yes.
Launch with intent.
Deliver an experience that exceeds expectations.
Then optimize based on real data and scale.

Average offers compete.
Strong offers convert.
Great offers dominate.

This likely happened when you were young:

You weren't able to recall ideas from books you were made to read in school

You were studying for an exam, but forgot everything before a test

Then teacher notices and drills this in your head:

"Reread it, and repeat it until it sticks"

As simple as that, now you've got memory all wrong.

An idea is planted: "If I can't memorize this by repetition, there's something wrong with me"

That's false.

You may forget where you leave things

You may even forget people's names..

Then you tell yourself these stories:

"I'm not good at remembering names...

I always forget them...

I'm a forgetful person..."

99% of the time, there's nothing wrong with your brain,

And being "forgetful" isn't a personality trait

This is also false.

And we're taught these false narrative since we're young

We take them as granted, never dare to question them and become self-fulfilling stories

The problem is we're taught passive learning as a default.

And we're measuring up to a standard that isn't even real!

"Moonwalking with Einstein" by Joshua Foer goes deeper into how memory actually works (and what your brain is capable of when you stop treating it like a hard drive).

Follow us (@collectivewisdomco) to read more and scroll less.

#reading #books #activrecall #readingtips #bookstagram #collectivewisdom

Fingerprint scanners 👆 are biometric systems that identify you using unique patterns on your fingers.
.
Every fingerprint has ridges, valleys, and minutiae points that are nearly impossible to replicate.
.
1️⃣ Capture — sensor takes an image or reads the fingerprint pattern
2️⃣ Types — optical (light), capacitive (electric charge), ultrasonic (sound waves)
3️⃣ Feature Extraction — key points like ridge endings & bifurcations are detected
4️⃣ Template Creation — fingerprint data is converted into a digital map
5️⃣ Matching — scanned print is compared with stored template for verification
.
It doesn’t store your actual fingerprint image — only a mathematical representation.
That’s why it’s fast, secure, and widely used in phones and security systems.
.
.
.

I have two boys with ADHD and personally, I’ve seen how much their behaviour, focus and mood shift depending on what they eat, how they sleep, and how supported their bodies actually are. It’s not perfect and honestly, it’s impossible for them to eat like this all the time. Life happens, parties happen, school happens. But what I’ve realised is that having an influence on what they eat at home can make the world of difference. When we focus on real food, enough protein, minerals like magnesium and iron, probiotics for gut health (remember the gut-brain axis), healthy fats which feed the brain and help manage blood sugar, and getting them to wind down properly at night (which is a mission on its own 😅), things feel calmer and more manageable. I’m not saying this replaces anything or works overnight, but small changes at home really do add up more than you think.

#adhdkids #mentalhealth #modernparenting #trendingnow #kidshealth
If only more parents implemented a proper human diet with their children they’d be thriving

日本利用压电瓷砖将脚步转化为电能。这些瓷砖捕捉来自你脚步的动能。当你行走时，你的重量和动作会对瓷砖产生压力。瓷砖会轻微弯曲，从而产生机械应力。瓷砖内部的压电材料将这种应力转化为电能。每一步都会产生少量电荷，而数百万步结合在一起就能产生足够的电力来驱动LED灯、数字显示屏和传感器。在像涩谷车站这样繁忙的地方，每天大约有240万个脚步为这一系统作出贡献。这些电能可以被储存或立即使用，从而减少对传统电力来源的依赖，并支持可持续的城市基础设施。这种方法将日常运动转化为实用的可再生能源#日本#知识#事实 #你知道吗#推荐科技创新历史 技术 实验 热门

George Santayana (1863-1952) was a Spanish-American philosopher, essayist, poet, and novelist. Born in Madrid, he was educated in the United States and spent much of his career teaching at Harvard University. Santayana is best known for his works on philosophy, aesthetics, and culture, including The Life of Reason. He emphasized the importance of critical thinking and intellectual independence. Though deeply influenced by classical philosophy, he maintained a skeptical and naturalistic outlook. Later in life, he returned to Europe, living in Italy until his death. His writings continue to influence modern thought and education.

Leo Tolstoy (1828-1910) was a renowned Russian novelist, philosopher, and social reformer, widely regarded as one of the greatest writers in world literature. He is best known for his epic novels War and Peace and Anna Karenina, which explore human emotions, society, and morality. Born into aristocratic family, Tolstoy later adopted a simple, spiritual lifestyle and promoted nonviolence and truth. His ideas influenced figures like Mahatma Gandhi. Through his works and philosophy, Tolstoy left a lasting impact on literature, ethics, and social thought worldwide.

Most people say they want to become more educated, but then spend hours consuming things that leave no real trace. Not because they lack discipline, but because they never replace the habit with something better.

There are certain topics that, once you understand them, change how you see everything else. You start to recognize patterns in history, understand why economies move the way they do, and see that many decisions, both personal and global, follow structures that repeat over time.

The difference is subtle at first. You begin to ask better questions, notice connections others overlook, and slowly develop a way of thinking that feels more clear and grounded. Over time, this compounds into something far more valuable than short bursts of information.

Becoming educated is not about knowing everything. It is about knowing the right things, the ones that actually help you understand the world instead of just reacting to it.
